setter.name: Derek
setter.evidence: I heard a lot of things already from Derek, but I would just love to go through it with you

prospect.name: Brandon Blair
prospect.occupation: Costco employee, recently moved into a new position; aiming for management
prospect.family_status: Engaged; fiancee approximately seven weeks pregnant with their first child
prospect.training_background: Martial arts since age 15 with a long-standing one-to-one sensei; roughly six weeks of calisthenics recently; gym with his father in high school. Owns four kettlebells (26, 35, 44, 53 lb).
prospect.medical: Left wrist pain when a kettlebell contacts the wrist during overhead pressing; self-suspected, undiagnosed: 'I think I have, I don't know what the hell it is, maybe psoriatic arthritis or something like that in it'.

signals: Proposed label: aspirational_low_liquidity — fits the physical and motivational profile of an optimizer (trained, disciplined, wants good to great) but has roughly $50 available and $150-200 monthly discretionary income, with a first child due.
Physically capable and self-directed: martial arts since 15, already owns four kettlebells and has been running calisthenics.
Zero value resistance and high stated intent throughout; the only blocker at any point was liquidity.
Not the_optimizer because price was an absolute barrier, not a quality signal; not skeptical_bargain_hunter because he never argued the offer was overpriced.

goals.text: Get shredded and lean enough to show a six-pack without flexing
Develop his legs so his lower body matches his upper body
Learn the full A-to-Z process himself so he can cut and bulk on his own for life
Be a father his child looks up to once the baby arrives
Pass the knowledge on to his fiancee and to people at work
Build the daily discipline and structure that would get him promoted into Costco management

pains.text: Doing kettlebell work self-taught and getting it wrong; the bell strikes his left wrist on overhead presses and hurts
Left wrist pain during loaded overhead work, self-suspected as psoriatic arthritis and never diagnosed
Learned to train from his father without ever being told why, so he never got the full picture
Approximately $50 available now and $150-200 discretionary per month, with a baby due
Carries visible belly fat under his shirt and notices it when he undresses

objections.raw_quote: So would I have to drop that full six grand right here, right now?
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection ('outside of the money aspects, just to see if it actually makes sense'), then asked what was available now and what was left over monthly.

objections.raw_quote: I would say probably 50 bucks, to be completely honest.
objections.rep_response: Asked about monthly leftovers, then floated third-party financing and asked for his credit score.

objections.raw_quote: If it comes down to it, it's a little too expensive or something along those lines. I get it. I'm sure I can find something different, you know, for maybe a little bit cheaper or something.
objections.rep_response: Did not defend the value; moved to a credit-score probe and then withdrew the offer.

objections.raw_quote: maybe I'll have to do it later on. When I'm more financially stable, you know, something along those lines
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the delay and confirmed he would not recommend proceeding now.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No plan was structured. The rep said 'most clients pay upfront, but it's not like...' and then offered third-party financing described as 'not taking out a loan', which the prospect refused.

evidence: The rep disqualified on affordability: 'Yeah, then I'm just going to be honest on this. I would not do this for now. I would just not even recommend it. I wouldn't even recommend you taking a loan for it.'
Prospect disclosed roughly $50 available and $150-200 monthly discretionary income with a first child due.
Counter-evidence: intent was total and never wavered — 'Oh, 100%. I want to get started. Yeah. Guaranteed.'

Counter-evidence: the call did not end in a flat no. The rep pivoted to a $200/month group community and the prospect said 'yeah, that sounds good', with a signup link to be sent. No payment was taken and no commitment was made, so the six-month offer is recorded as lost.
Counter-evidence for the sales record: this is a refused core offer with a live downsell, not a clean loss.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a free training video plus a signup link for the $200/month group community; check back in after the prospect's next paycheck and revisit one-to-one coaching once he reaches Costco management.

notable.note: Two things a manager should see. First, the rep described third-party financing to a former banking-industry employee as 'not taking out a loan... It takes a little bit on your credit, but it doesn't really take out a loan or anything', and the prospect corrected him. Second, the rep improvised a $200/month or $2,000/year community tier that sits outside the stated $6,000/$9,000 offer. Separately, the prospect disclosed suspected psoriatic arthritis causing wrist pain during overhead kettlebell work and the rep answered 'it's an easy fix, that's a form fix' without asking whether anyone had looked at it.

quality.notes: Heavy and continuous label inversion. Long passages of the prospect's speech are attributed to Richard Claessen and vice versa — for example the 'hidden strength' answer at 00:03:27, the six-pack line at 00:06:51, the fiancee-pregnancy exchange at 00:17:50, and most of the closing sequence from 00:52:25 onward. Role was read from content throughout; the rep is whoever is running discovery and presenting.
